story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Drag-and-drop file uploader with inline image/PDF preview, download button for all file types; unsupported file types blocked and attempt logged. 2. Attachments stored in Supabase Storage with randomized file names (UUID-based paths), metadata (filename, mimeType, fileSize) stored in database; access limited by company_id. 3. Each download/view/delete action logged in audit with: user ID, timestamp, IP address (if available). 4. Delete allowed only for vouchers with status=DRAFT and by creator or admin role; requires confirmation modal with mandatory reason field. 5. Download links are signed URLs with 10-minute expiry; URLs generated on-demand via Supabase Storage API. 6. Simulated virus scan triggered on upload (mock validation); blocks file type if scan fails, logs failure. 7. Voucher icon/badge always displays current attachment count; click opens attachment management modal. 8. File upload handles large files via multi-part upload, robust to network errors (retry logic, progress indicator).

doc.title: Epic 3: Voucher Engine & General Ledger Core
doc.snippet: As an accountant, I want to upload and manage voucher attachments for compliance, so that all supporting documentation is always available, secure, and auditable. Acceptance criteria include drag-and-drop uploader, Supabase Storage with randomized paths, audit logging, delete restrictions, signed URLs, virus scan simulation, attachment count badge, and robust file upload handling.

doc.title: Story 3.5: Audit Trail for Voucher Lifecycle
doc.snippet: Comprehensive audit logging infrastructure available for reuse. AuditLogService patterns for attachment events. VoucherAuditHelper for JSON serialization and SHA-256 hash calculation. VoucherHistoryService for history retrieval with field-by-field diff generation.

doc.title: Story 3.3: Posting, Unposting & Reversal Workflows
doc.snippet: Atomic transaction management using @Transactional annotation. Error handling patterns with detailed error messages. RBAC enforcement patterns: @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('ACCOUNTANT','CHIEF_ACCOUNTANT','ADMIN','CFO')") for upload/view endpoints.

doc.title: Story 3.4: Leaf-Only and Double-Entry Validation Engine
doc.snippet: Return detailed field-level error maps for validation failures, not generic 400 errors. Follow ValidationErrorMap pattern from VoucherValidationService for file type, size, virus scan validation errors.

doc.title: Story 3.6: Period Selector & Voucher-Period Mapping
doc.snippet: Follow clean separation of concerns pattern from PeriodManagementService. Create VoucherAttachmentService interface with clear responsibilities: file upload, download, delete, signed URL generation. Company scoping enforced via CompanyContext.

doc.title: Data Architecture
doc.snippet: Row-level filtering via company_id on all tables. Spring Data JPA filter at repository level. API-level enforcement via security filter. Supabase RLS policies as additional layer.

doc.title: Security Architecture
doc.snippet: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Admin, Accountant, Chief Accountant, CFO. Spring Security method-level security. API-level permission checks. Company-level data isolation.

constraint.description: Follow feature-first structure: Place AttachmentDropzone component under frontend/src/components/voucher/ for shared use across voucher screens. Backend API endpoints follow REST convention /api/v1/vouchers/{voucherId}/attachments with standard response format { data: VoucherAttachmentDTO[], meta: {...} }.

All attachment operations enforce company-level isolation via company_id filtering. RBAC: Accountant+ can upload/view attachments, only creator or admin can delete. Use @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('ACCOUNTANT','CHIEF_ACCOUNTANT','ADMIN','CFO')") for upload/view endpoints, additional check for delete.

Use @Transactional annotation for attachment operations that involve multiple steps (upload + metadata save, delete + storage cleanup) to ensure all-or-nothing execution. Follow pattern from VoucherPostingService.postVoucher() for atomic operations.

Return detailed error messages for blocked operations (e.g., "Cannot delete attachment: voucher is posted", "File type not supported: .exe"). Return detailed field-level error maps for validation failures (file type, size, virus scan), not generic 400 errors. Follow error response format from VoucherPostingService and ValidationErrorMap pattern from VoucherValidationService.

Follow comprehensive testing approach from Story 3.3: integration tests with @SpringBootTest, unit tests for service layer, negative test scenarios for blocked operations, RBAC testing with different role combinations. Test organization by acceptance criteria with clear mapping between ACs and test classes.

Attachments stored in Supabase Storage with randomized UUID-based file paths (vouchers/{voucherId}/{uuid}-{filename}) to prevent enumeration. Metadata (filename, mimeType, fileSize) stored in database for efficient querying. Signed URLs with 10-minute expiry generated on-demand via Supabase Storage API.

File type whitelist: PDF, images (JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP). File size limit: 10MB max per file (configurable). Virus scan simulation: mock validation on upload, blocks file if scan fails, logs failure. All validation errors shown at once (bulk validation).

All attachment operations (download, view, delete) logged in audit trail with user ID, timestamp, IP address, and file metadata. Follow AuditLogService patterns from Story 3.5. Include action type (DOWNLOAD/VIEW/DELETE), user/role, device/IP, timestamp, file metadata in audit logs.

tests.standards: Testing patterns derived from established practices in previous Epic 3 stories (Stories 3.3-3.6). Use @SpringBootTest with IntegrationTest base class for API endpoint tests, covering RBAC enforcement, company scoping, file upload/download, signed URL generation, and audit logging. Create unit tests for service layer file handling logic, following patterns from VoucherValidationService tests for validation and error map generation. Include negative test scenarios for blocked operations (e.g., delete on posted voucher, unsupported file type, size violation, virus scan failure), following the pattern from VoucherPostingService tests. Organize tests by acceptance criteria, with clear mapping between ACs and test classes. Frontend testing follows component testing patterns from Story 3.6's PeriodSelector component tests, demonstrating proper TypeScript typing, error handling, and user interaction testing.

idea.description: Test drag-and-drop file upload: simulate drag events, verify file validation (type, size), test preview for images and PDFs, test download button functionality, test error display for unsupported file types, verify unsupported file type attempts are logged in audit.

Test Supabase Storage integration: verify randomized UUID-based file paths (vouchers/{voucherId}/{uuid}-{filename}), test metadata storage in database (filename, mimeType, fileSize), verify company_id filtering, test cross-company access blocked (404 Not Found).

Test audit logging: verify download events logged with user ID, timestamp, IP address, file metadata; verify view events (preview) logged; verify delete events logged with reason; test audit log entry format matches specification.

Test delete restrictions: verify delete blocked for posted vouchers (403 Forbidden), verify delete blocked for non-creator/non-admin users (403 Forbidden), verify delete allowed for draft vouchers by creator, verify delete allowed for draft vouchers by admin, test confirmation modal with mandatory reason field, verify reason captured in audit log.

Test signed URL generation: verify signed URLs generated on-demand, test 10-minute expiry (wait 11 minutes, verify URL expired), test URL regeneration for new download requests, verify signed URLs are unique per request.

Test virus scan simulation: verify mock scan triggered on upload, test file type blocking (e.g., .exe files blocked), verify scan failure logged in audit trail with file metadata, test error message format: "File failed virus scan: {filename}".

Test attachment count badge: verify badge displays current attachment count on VoucherList and VoucherForm, test badge click opens attachment management modal, verify badge updates after upload/delete operations, test badge visibility (always visible).

Test multi-part upload and network error handling: test large file upload (>10MB) with multi-part support, verify progress indicator displays during upload, test retry logic (3 retries with exponential backoff), test network error recovery (simulate network failure, verify retry), test browser crash/network interruption handling.

Negative test scenarios: delete on posted voucher (403 Forbidden), unsupported file type upload (400 Bad Request with error message), file size violation (400 Bad Request), virus scan failure (400 Bad Request), cross-company access (404 Not Found), non-creator/non-admin delete attempt (403 Forbidden), missing reason field on delete (400 Bad Request).

End-to-end workflow test: upload attachment → preview attachment → download attachment → delete attachment (with reason). Verify all steps work together, audit logs captured for each step, UI updates correctly after each operation.
